name: Motorcycle
description: A motor vehicle with a seat or saddle designed to travel on no more than three wheels, excluding electric bicycles, electric scooters and mopeds: an electric two-wheeler over 1,500 W or faster than 30 mph is one. Nevada law doesn't define an electric motorcycle separately. Defined by Nevada Revised Statutes §486.041 and §482.070.
restrictions: A seat or saddle and no more than three wheels on the ground
No limit on motor power or speed
One designed primarily for off-highway use and not registered for the road is an off-highway vehicle instead
Riders need a motorcycle driver's license or a driver's license endorsed for motorcycles; a motorcycle license applicant must be 18, or 16 to 17 meeting the young-driver requirements
Riders and passengers must wear a helmet, plus glasses, goggles or a face shield unless a windscreen meeting DMV standards protects them
Registered with the DMV, and the owner must carry liability insurance
No lane splitting: it can't ride between vehicles in adjacent lanes, though two motorcycles may share a lane
